2608.14354.title: ScienceFlow: A long-horizon agent for ML research, scientific discovery and beyond
2608.14354.paper_summary: Enabling LLM agents to sustain productive, stable, and goal-aligned research over extended horizons is a central challenge for autonomous machine learning and scientific discovery, as progress hinges on continuously managing evolving state, exploration decisions, and computational resources. Pioneering autoresearch agents, despite great success, still lack mechanisms for continuity, recovery from dead ends, and value-driven compute allocation, which inherently undermines overall search efficiency, wastes computational resources, and lowers the chance of ultimate success. To bridge this gap, we introduce ScienceFlow, an end-to-end autoresearch agent framework that organizes long-horizon research work into research segments grounded in executable workspaces. It represents research progress as recoverable executable states, enabling efficient exploration, revision, and execution. Transitions between research segments are governed by Executable-State Transition through Re-Anchoring (ESTRA), which selects either the live state or an archived state as the next anchor and determines whether to continue or redirect the research trajectory. An evidence-aware execution controller allocates resources to physical jobs based on resource availability, remaining budget, and validated progress. We evaluate ScienceFlow on tasks spanning machine learning, scientific modeling, and mathematical optimization. Results on diverse long-horizon benchmarks demonstrate its ability to sustain effective research processes, highlighted by a SOTA 70.22 percent Any-Medal score on the full MLE-bench within a 24-hour budget, outperforming prior reported results by 4.92 percentage points. The efficacy of ScienceFlow further demonstrates that efficient state management, adaptive exploration, and objective-aligned execution are critical for scaling autonomous research beyond short-horizon interactions.
2608.14354.paper_summary_zh: 使 LLM 代理能夠在長期內持續進行富有成效、穩定且目標一致的研究，是自動化機器學習和科學發現的一個核心挑戰，因為進展依賴於不斷管理不斷演變的狀態、探索決策和計算資源。儘管開創性的自動研究代理取得了巨大成功，但仍然缺乏連續性、從死胡同中恢復和基於價值的計算資源分配的機制，這本質上削弱了整體搜索效率，浪費了計算資源，並降低了最終成功的機會。為了填補這一空白，我們介紹了 ScienceFlow，一個端到端的自動研究代理框架，將長期研究工作組織成基於可執行工作空間的研究片段。它將研究進展表示為可恢復的可執行狀態，從而實現高效的探索、修訂和執行。研究片段之間的轉換由可執行狀態過渡通過重新錨定（ESTRA）來管理，該過程選擇當前狀態或存檔狀態作為下一個錨點，並決定是否繼續或重新導向研究軌跡。一個基於證據的執行控制器根據資源可用性、剩餘預算和驗證進展來分配資源給實際工作。我們在涵蓋機器學習、科學建模和數學優化的任務上評估了 ScienceFlow。在多樣化的長期基準測試中的結果顯示其能夠持續有效的研究過程，特別是在 24 小時預算內的完整 MLE-bench 上達到 SOTA 70.22% 的任何獎牌分數，超越了之前報告的結果 4.92 個百分點。ScienceFlow 的有效性進一步證明，高效的狀態管理、自適應探索和目標一致的執行對於擴展自主研究超越短期互動至關重要。
